around.headline: Delivery rider thrashed with a wooden stick by unidentified group
around.summary: A delivery agent — later identified as a Zepto rider — was beaten with a wooden stick by an unidentified group in Bengaluru today; the rider alleges he was abused for not speaking Hindi, and a case has been registered. If you work a delivery job or manage one, know that platforms have in-app SOS options, and any assault should be reported to police immediately rather than settled on the street.
around.source: The Times of India, NDTV, The New Indian Express

around.headline: KSRTC bus overturns on Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway, driver and conductor killed
around.summary: A KSRTC bus overturned on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway today, killing the driver and conductor; reports put the number of injured passengers anywhere from about 14 to 25 depending on the source and time of reporting. If you're booked on an intercity bus this weekend, take the seatbelt if one's fitted and avoid the front-most seats where possible.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: Food-safety crackdown widens from star hotels to supply centres
around.summary: After raids turned up rotten vegetables, expired milk and fungal produce at Bengaluru's 5-star (and now some 3-star) hotel kitchens, the FDA has started inspecting the food supply centres and vendors that stock them. If you eat out often, it's worth asking a restaurant for its current FSSAI hygiene rating before you book a table this week.
around.source: The Times of India, NDTV, The Indian Express

around.headline: 'Operation Mukta': ~500 police across 50 locations checking for illegal immigrants
around.summary: Bengaluru police have deployed roughly 500 personnel across 50 locations under 'Operation Mukta', detaining close to 1,900 people so far, including at least 15 confirmed Bangladeshi nationals. If you're stopped for an identity check as part of this drive, carrying a valid photo ID — Aadhaar, voter ID or passport — will save you time.

around.headline: Bill in Parliament could bar under-13s from social media and gaming accounts
around.summary: A bill introduced in Parliament today proposes barring children under 13 from creating accounts on social media and gaming platforms. If you have kids that age with existing accounts, it's a good moment to review what personal data those accounts already hold, since stricter age-verification is likely coming.

street_smart.title: An unknown number messages just 'Hi', then starts video-calling you back to back — and when you pick up, it turns into obscene content. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru incident: an accountant reported receiving obscene video calls from an unknown man whose contact started with a friendly 'Hi' message (The Times of India). This is a different mechanism from the sextortion/blackmail scenario used on 2026-07-23 — there's no prior online relationship being built and no money is being demanded, so the correct response differs (report-and-block, not preserve-evidence-for-a-ransom-negotiation). No street-smart topic in the last 3 weeks has covered unsolicited obscene calls from a stranger.
street_smart.situation: A number you don't recognise texts just 'Hi', then starts calling you on video repeatedly. Curious or thinking it might be a wrong number, you pick up — and the call turns out to be obscene. The calls keep coming.

choices.text: Pick up again to see if you recognise his voice or face, hoping to identify who it is.
choices.feedback: Risky. Answering again only exposes you to more of the same content and tells the caller you're engaging — it doesn't reliably reveal who they are, since caller ID on an unknown SIM tells you nothing useful.

choices.text: Block the number straight away without saving anything.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Blocking feels like the responsible instinct, but do it first and you lose the number, the message thread and the call log — exactly the evidence a cybercrime complaint needs. The caller can simply resurface on a new SIM and target someone else with no record ever existing.

choices.text: Reply telling him to stop, or ask why he's doing this.
choices.feedback: Risky. Any reply, even an angry one, confirms the number is active and being read, which tends to invite more attempts rather than fewer — harassers often escalate when they get a reaction.

choices.text: Screenshot the number, the 'Hi' message and the call log, then block the number and report it via cybercrime.gov.in or the national helpline 1930, following up with a local police complaint if it continues.
choices.feedback: Correct. Capturing the evidence before blocking means you can actually file a complaint that identifies the number and pattern of contact. Obscene calls and unsolicited explicit content are covered under India's laws on outraging a person's modesty and obscenity, and the cybercrime portal is built specifically to escalate this kind of report.

takeaways: Screenshot the number, the message and the call log before you block — that record is what turns a complaint into something police or the cybercrime portal can actually act on.
Report through cybercrime.gov.in or call the National Cyber Crime Helpline, 1930 — don't rely on blocking alone, since it doesn't stop the caller from targeting someone else next.
Don't reply, even to tell them off — silence plus a report is more effective than engagement, which tends to encourage repeat contact.

quiz.question: What happened to a KSRTC bus on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway today?
options: It overturned, killing the driver and conductor and injuring several passengers
It caught fire at a toll plaza with no injuries
It was involved in a minor collision with no casualties
It broke down, stranding passengers for six hours
quiz.why: Reports on the number of injured passengers varied between roughly 14 and 25 depending on the source and time of reporting.

quiz.question: Roughly how many police personnel and locations are involved in Bengaluru's 'Operation Mukta' crackdown on illegal immigrants?
quiz.why: The drive has detained close to 1,900 people so far, including at least 15 confirmed Bangladeshi nationals.

quiz.question: What does a bill introduced in Parliament today propose regarding children under 13?
options: Barring them from creating accounts on social media and gaming platforms
Requiring them to pass a digital literacy test before using the internet
Making schools responsible for issuing verified digital IDs to minors
quiz.why: The move reflects growing global regulatory pressure on platforms to verify users' ages before letting them sign up.

quiz.question: In India's Parliament, which house is known as the 'Council of States'?
quiz.why: Unlike the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body — a third of its members retire every two years instead of the whole house facing election together.

quiz.question: Which organ in the human body regulates blood sugar by producing insulin and glucagon?
quiz.why: The pancreas is both an endocrine gland (hormones like insulin) and an exocrine gland (digestive enzymes released into the small intestine).
